item.title: Caitlin Clark shines, but Fever suffer embarrassing blowout loss to Mystics as playoff race heats up
item.description: Caitlin Clark scored 25 points but the Indiana Fever fell 93-77 to the Washington Mystics, slipping behind the Atlanta Dream for fourth seeding.
item.content:encoded:
You have to hate Sunday's performance if you're an Indiana Fever fan.

The Fever seemed to join Week 2 of the NFL in a scoring slump on Sunday, falling to the Washington Mystics 93-77 in a one-sided loss with real playoff implications on the line. The defeat extinguished much of the Fever's late-season momentum.

A squad of Fever veterans got thoroughly outplayed by a youth-heavy Washington roster. (Fever fans, you know how this looks, right? Not great.)

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Caitlin Clark, as expected, led all scorers with 25 points and added five assists, though she also committed five turnovers. Clark and Kelsey Mitchell were the only real sparks for the Fever on Sunday, accounting for 47 of their 77 points.

Not even a home-court advantage could elevate the Fever in a miserable all-around outing.

The Washington game was crucial for the Fever, who slipped a game behind the Atlanta Dream for fourth seeding.

Indiana leaned on the perimeter early, but went 0-for-7 from deep to open the game. Sophie Cunningham, one of the league's top three-point shooters, played just four minutes in the first half as Indiana fell into a 51-30 hole at the break.

FEVER COACH STEPHANIE WHITE OPENS UP ABOUT FAN RECEPTION AFTER TURBULENT WEEK OF WNBA CONTROVERSY

Washington eventually stretched its lead to 26. Indiana trimmed that deficit to 14 in the third quarter, but that was the best push the Fever could muster against a Mystics team featuring more than half its roster in their first or second year.

With two upcoming games against the league-best Minnesota Lynx, the pressure is on coach Stephanie White and the Fever to shake off Sunday's ugly loss and deliver a statement before the postseason.

The Fever's first game out of the FIBA break saw them notch an 18-point win over the struggling Toronto Tempo. Sunday's loss wiped away that momentum, but knocking off the Lynx would certainly boost morale in Indy, and then some.

item.title: Washington Commanders face season-defining crisis as Jayden Daniels suffers another serious elbow injury
item.description: Jayden Daniels was carted off at halftime after appearing to dislocate his left elbow on the final play of the half against the Dallas Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was carted off the field at halftime during Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys after he appeared to injure his left elbow on the final play of the first half.

During the play, he seemed to hyperextend the left elbow. And, yes, it was ugly.

It happened on the final play of the first half when Daniels pulled away from center but tripped. As he tried to regain his balance, he used his left arm to hold himself up.

COMMANDERS OFFENSE TAKES MAJOR HIT AS STAR OFFENSIVE TACKLE SUFFERS MAJOR TRAINING CAMP INJURY

The elbow gave way in a manner it is not supposed to bend.

KYLER MURRAY KNOCKED OUT OF VIKINGS DEBUT AFTER FOREARM TO THE HELMET AND BLOW TO NECK BY TWO PACKERS

And all this is terrible news because Daniels had a similar injury in 2025 against the Seattle Seahawks.

So this very easily could be a season-defining injury for Daniels. And the Commanders.

Again.

OutKick medical expert Dr. David Chao, who served 17 seasons as the head physician for the then-San Diego Chargers and currently runs the Sports Injury Central website, studied the injury via tape. He put out a post on X with his view.

"By video, clear left elbow dislocation...

"Similar to last season

"Joint comes out easier second time original ligament tear heals "looser."

Although the injury was to his arm, Daniels was carted off to the locker room. He wore a towel over his head, apparently, to avoid showing his facial reaction to the crowd.

Daniels has been replaced, at least for the remainder of this game, by backup quarterback Marcus Mariota.

And if this injury is what everyone's eyes are seeing, the Washington Commanders' season is on the brink in only the second week of the season.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

If Daniels faces a similar situation to last season, he faces a similar rehabilitation.

Daniels dislocated his left elbow while scrambling in Washington’s Week 9 loss to Seattle on Nov. 2, 2025. An MRI found no fracture or ligament damage, so he avoided surgery and was not placed on injured reserve.

He returned in Week 14 against Minnesota but aggravated the elbow, was not cleared for the following game and was shut down for the final three weeks of the season as the Commanders prioritized his recovery for 2026.

That recovery appears to be derailed at least for the short term.

item.title: Jets collapse late against Packers, miss chance at first 2-0 start since 2015 in overtime loss
item.description: The New York Jets blew a 17-7 fourth quarter lead as the Green Bay Packers scored 13 unanswered points to win 20-17 in overtime at MetLife Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
For most of Sunday afternoon, the New York Jets looked poised to move to 2-0 for the first time since 2015. The Jets controlled most of the game against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium, but made some crucial errors down the stretch to cough up their 10-point fourth-quarter lead.

The Packers scored 13 unanswered points to win 20-17 in overtime, with Trey Smack kicking a 26-yard field goal to complete the comeback.

Green Bay struck first on a 6-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to MarShawn Lloyd in the second quarter, but the Jets answered with a 5-yard touchdown run from Braelon Allen. Geno Smith connected with Garrett Wilson for a 5-yard score in the third quarter to give New York a 14-7 lead.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Jets appeared to have delivered the knockout blow early in the fourth quarter when they recovered a Lloyd fumble at the Green Bay 18-yard line. But the offense couldn't move the ball and settled for a 32-yard Jason Sanders field goal, extending the lead to 17-7 with 11:04 remaining.

That's when everything started to unravel.

A 38-yard pass-interference penalty helped Green Bay march down the field before Love found Christian Watson for a 3-yard touchdown. The Jets failed to pick up a first down on their next possession, and Skyy Moore returned the ensuing punt 63 yards to the New York 19-yard line. Smack kicked a 34-yard field goal four plays later to tie the game.

New York still had a chance to win in regulation. After Breece Hall gained just one yard on third-and-2, the Jets faced fourth-and-1 at midfield with 1:20 remaining. Aaron Glenn kept his offense on the field rather than punting, an aggressive decision to try to win the game. It's hard to fault Glenn for trusting his offense to gain one yard, but Braelon Allen was stuffed. Green Bay failed to capitalize, sending the game to overtime.

The Jets received the ball first in overtime and the possession was a complete disaster. The Packers sacked Smith on consecutive plays, the offense committed a false-start penalty and New York faced a third-and-30 from their own 10-yard line before eventually punting on fourth down.

Green Bay then moved 58 yards on four offensive plays, aided by an unnecessary roughness penalty against Jarvis Brownlee Jr., before Smack ended the game on the fifth play of the drive.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Penalties were a problem for both teams throughout the game. Green Bay was flagged 14 times for 133 yards, while New York committed 13 penalties for 156 yards. That's an absurd 27 accepted penalties for 289 yards.

But the timing of the Jets' two biggest penalties proved especially costly: the 38-yard pass-interference call aided Green Bay's fourth-quarter touchdown drive, while Brownlee's 15-yard penalty moved the Packers into position for the winning field goal.

Smith completed 27-of-41 passes for 247 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. It wasn't a spectacular performance, but it should have been good enough given how well New York's defense played.

That's what makes the loss particularly brutal for the Jets. New York outgained Green Bay 285-199, held the Packers to 1-of-9 on third down, won the turnover battle and possessed the ball for nearly 11 minutes longer. Love threw for just 145 yards, although he threw two touchdowns and avoided turning the ball over.

The Jets had the game won and a chance to send the MetLife Stadium crowd home believing in a 2-0 team. Instead, they gave the game away and sent their fans home wondering how they managed to blow another one.

item.title: Mike Vrabel snaps at reporter over Drake Maye's struggles after Pats win: 'you're not going to ruin my Sunday'
item.description: Mike Vrabel told reporters they wouldn't ruin his Sunday after the Patriots beat the Steelers 20-3, but Drake Maye's struggles still loom large.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots got their first win of the season Sunday, and head coach Mike Vrabel wasn't about to let a few perfectly valid questions about his quarterback spoil the celebration.

After New England defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 20-3, Vrabel had a tense exchange with Boston Globe reporter Ben Volin, who pressed him about his level of concern over Drake Maye's performance through the first two weeks of the season.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Vrabel wasn't interested in entertaining the question.

"You're not going to ruin my Sunday," the coach fired back.

The exchange continued when reporter Greg Bedard also questioned Vrabel about Maye's struggles, prompting the coach to make it clear that he wasn't going to dwell on the negatives after a victory.

To be fair, though, the reporters had a legitimate reason to ask.

Maye hasn't exactly looked like the quarterback who led New England to the Super Bowl last season, and Sunday's win over Pittsburgh did little to put those concerns to rest.

The 23-year-old completed 14 of 22 passes for 208 yards, no touchdowns and one interception against the Steelers. While he connected with receiver Romeo Doubs for a 63-yard gain, the Patriots struggled to consistently move the ball and finished with just 13 offensive points.

Instead, New England's defense did most of the heavy lifting, holding Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers to just 3 points and 235 total yards.

Rookie running back TreVeyon Henderson provided the Patriots' only offensive touchdown with a 39-yard run in the first quarter. Later, Christian Barmore strip-sacked Rodgers, and Elijah Ponder returned the fumble 19 yards for a touchdown to put the game away.

In other words, the Patriots won comfortably, but Maye wasn't exactly the reason why.

Sunday's performance came just 11 days after a disastrous season opener against the Seattle Seahawks.

In a rematch of Super Bowl LX, Maye threw three fourth-quarter interceptions as New England blew a 10-point lead and lost 13-10. His final interception came in the end zone with just 26 seconds remaining, ending a potential game-tying drive.

Maye finished that game with 178 passing yards, one touchdown and three interceptions. Afterward, he acknowledged that he had abandoned the patient approach that had worked earlier in the game.

"We had the game under control," Maye said following the loss. "Thought we had a good plan to start chipping away and be patient and lost patience, and it cost us, decisions that cost us the game on my part, on my end."

Through two games, Maye has thrown four interceptions and just one touchdown pass.

That's a far cry from his 2025 campaign, when he threw for 4,394 yards and 31 touchdowns while finishing as the runner-up in NFL MVP voting.

Vrabel is certainly entitled to enjoy Sunday's victory, especially after the Patriots' ugly collapse against Seattle.

Sure, the season is young. No need to overreact.

But with New England's franchise quarterback — so far — struggling to recapture last year's form, the questions about his performance aren't going away simply because Vrabel wants them to.

item.title: Converse pulls latest shoes ad after critics accuse of sharing 'racist' and 'reckless' KKK imagery
item.description: Converse pulled a shoe ad last week after critics said the imagery resembled a Ku Klux Klan hood and a lynching victim, prompting a public apology and statement.
item.content:encoded:
Converse apologized and pulled a shoe ad last week that some claimed featured Ku Klux Klan imagery.

The ad, which has been removed from the Nike subsidiary's social media pages, featured K-pop singer Karina of the girl group aespa promoting the Chuck 70 X and Run Star Crush sneakers. In the ad, Karina held a pair of black high-top shoes under a star-shaped spotlight while wearing a long white skirt.

Several social media users asserted that Karina resembled a KKK member, with the shoes resembling a lynching victim. Critics included Rep. Troy Carter, D-La., who released a statement on the ad on Friday.

OUTKICK'S CRAIG CARTON REVEALS THE REAL REASON NIKE STOCK IS IN THE TANK: 'THEY'RE FAILING MISERABLY'

"Nike and Converse, what the hell were you thinking?" Carter said. "Your campaign shows what looks like a hooded Klansman, framed by what appears to be the dangling feet of a lynching victim. There is nothing creative or artistic about it. It is racist, reckless and deeply offensive."

After facing backlash, Converse eventually pulled the ad and released a statement apologizing for the campaign.

TED CRUZ TAKES VICTORY LAP AS ICONIC AMERICAN BRAND'S STOCK PLUNGES TO 12-YEAR LOW

"We’re sorry. We understand why this image is deeply upsetting and recognize that we got this wrong. We removed it from our channels and are working to remove it everywhere it appeared. This should not have happened, and we will do better," the statement sent to Fox News Digital read.

This latest ad backlash comes as Nike is set to be removed from the S&P 100 after nearly 18 years, following its value dropping by more than $200 billion since 2021.

Conservative critics have frequently accused Nike of embracing woke politics by partnering with progressive figures like Colin Kaepernick and Dylan Mulvaney. However, Nike has faced backlash from the left as well.

NIKE FORGOT THAT REPUBLICANS BUY SNEAKERS, TOO, AND NOW IT'S GETTING BOOTED FROM THE S&P 100

In April, Nike went viral with a Boston Marathon ad reading "Runners welcome. Walkers tolerated" which critics claimed was "pace-shaming" participants.

In a new comment to Fox News Digital, a Carter spokesperson said that the apology was not enough.

"An apology and the removal of the images are not enough. Nike and Converse must explain how this campaign was conceived and approved, identify those responsible, and commission an independent investigation. They must also disclose the process and establish safeguards to ensure that imagery invoking the Klan and the lynching of Black people is never approved again," Carter's office said.

item.title: Atlanta Falcons are dealing with the worst quarterback situation in the NFL and it isn't even close
item.description: Cooper Rush fumbled and threw two interceptions before Kevin Stefanski benched him, and his replacement threw a pick six in his Falcons debut.
item.content:encoded:
The worst quarterback situation in the NFL right now? The Atlanta Falcons.

And it isn't very close at all.

The Falcons on Sunday started third-stringer Cooper Rush for the second time this season while Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa were designated as inactive due to ongoing health issues.

Penix Jr. has been recovering from knee surgery following an ACL injury last season.

FALCONS QUARTERBACK PROBLEMS DEEPEN AS TUA TAGOVAILOA SUFFERS OBLIQUE STRAIN AT PRACTICE

And Tagovailoa was out for the second consecutive week after he suffered an unexpected oblique injury two weeks ago, this time in practice. Although no one touched him.

Anyway, Rush got the call and he promptly stunk.

Again.

On Atlanta's opening possession, Rush lost the ball on a fumble, which the Panthers recovered at the Atlanta 35-yard line. Carolina converted the turnover into a touchdown.

Rush threw an interception on the following series, then added a second one later in the game.

He completed 10 of 17 passes against the Panthers, which doesn't sound terrible except that you read the previous paragraphs that outlined Rush's, ahem, struggles with turnovers.

This followed a Week 1 performance against the Pittsburgh Steelers in which Rush also threw two interceptions.

"Obviously, extremely disappointed in that game and extremely disappointed in how that game started," Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said. "And then [we] could not crawl out of that hole. And in the second half, it got away from us. So very disappointed.

"As you guys know, giveaways and takeaways are the key to this game and to turn it over that many times ... there's no way to win in the NFL like that."

Stefanski made those feelings known before he ever stepped up to the post-game microphones. Because he benched Rush before the end of the third quarter.

The coach had seen enough. Except the poor quarterback play was far from over.

Stefanski inserted fourth-string quarterback Jack Strand.

Strand threw an interception on his first pass attempt. And it wasn't just any interception. Strand threw a pick six when Devin Lloyd returned his pass 16 yards for a score.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

This is Keystone Cops type QB play. The Falcons are used to QB issues, but this is something else again.

The Falcons are hoping that can end by Thursday when they play the Green Bay Packers.

They're hoping Penix Jr., who has been practicing and ramping up toward game action, can start that in Wisconsin. They hope that Tagovailoa will ultimately decide he can tolerate some pain and take the field, or receive an injection to help him do so.

The Falcons are doing a lot of hoping about their quarterback room. And so far, it hasn't paid off.

item.title: Frankie Muniz describes hitting 'rock bottom' as estranged wife posts cryptic message about perspective
item.description: Frankie Muniz said the past six weeks have been a "nightmare" as he opened up about hitting rock bottom and doing the uncomfortable work ahead.
item.content:encoded:
Frankie Muniz revealed he recently hit "rock bottom," describing the past six weeks as an emotional "nightmare."

"The last 6 weeks of my life have been a nightmare I’m praying to wake up from. Everything felt heavy, unclear, and like it was falling apart at the same time," the "Malcolm in the Middle" star wrote on Instagram on Friday. "I wouldn’t wish this season on anyone."

"The unexpected gift in the middle of it is that I’ve had nowhere to hide," he continued. "I’ve had time to sit with myself, do real self-reflection, and finally see the areas of my life that need work if I want to become a better version of me. Not the polished version I show the world...the actual one."

JANA KRAMER SAYS HOLDING ON TO TOXIC RELATIONSHIPS 'DRAINS YOU' UNTIL YOU ‘START LOSING YOURSELF' COMPLETELY

Muniz said he read that "hitting rock bottom" in the one thing that can wake you up.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"It forces the changes you needed to make all along so you can live the best life possible," he wrote. "That idea has been sitting with me. In five years I believe I’ll look back at this exact low point and feel grateful for it, because the high I’ll be standing on then only exists because I went through this."

RELATIONSHIP EXPERT CHALLENGES ONE OF AMERICA'S BIGGEST ASSUMPTIONS ABOUT DIVORCE

"This isn’t the end of the story. It’s the part where I start doing the work...the uncomfortable, unglamorous, necessary work. I’m choosing to treat this season as the foundation, not the finish line," he continued.

"If you’re in a low place right now too, you’re not broken," he concluded. "You’re being rebuilt. Let's keep going!"

A representative for Muniz did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Shortly after Muniz’s post, his estranged wife, Paige Price, shared a cryptic message about "perspective."

"Life is all about perspective," Price wrote in an Instagram Story Friday, per Entertainment Weekly. "If you ask the grass, the zebra is the monster and the lion is the protector."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Price also shared a clip from a conversation between podcaster Jay Shetty and divorce lawyer James Sexton, in which Sexton said "the right thing to do is to do the hard thing."

Neither Muniz nor Price specified what prompted the posts.

AMANDA SEYFRIED AND THOMAS SADOSKI SAY SEPARATION IS 'RIGHT MOVE' FOR FAMILY AFTER NEARLY 10 YEARS OF MARRIAGE

The former couple later appeared to put on a united front during a family outing with their 5-year-old son, Mauz.

"Post soccer shenanigans with the fam. Our little dude got a medal for excellence in sportsmanship!" Muniz captioned a photo of himself, Price and their son, according to Entertainment Weekly.

Muniz and Price announced in July that they were ending their marriage after a private period of separation. The couple married in 2019 after being together for roughly a decade.

"After 10 beautiful years together, we’ve grown in ways that made us realize our relationship feels most natural and strong as a deep friendship and as co-parents," Muniz previously wrote on social media.

Although their romantic relationship has ended, Muniz said he remains grateful to Price for her support and sacrifices throughout their marriage. The pair also plans to continue co-parenting Mauz and running Muniz Racing together.

"I'm endlessly grateful to Paige for everything she's done for me and our family," Muniz previously wrote. "That foundation of respect and friendship isn’t going anywhere."

item.title: Jalen Hurts saves Eagles from ugly upset as Philadelphia escapes Titans to remain unbeaten
item.description: Jalen Hurts hit Darius Cooper for a last-second touchdown to erase a three-point deficit as the Philadelphia Eagles escaped Nashville 24-20.
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Eagles moved to 2-0 with a win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday afternoon in Nashville.

That's a sentence most football fans expected to read before the game even started. What most probably didn't expect was exactly what it took for the Eagles to go into Nissan Stadium and beat the Titans.

Jalen Hurts connected with Darius Cooper for a 3-yard touchdown with less than 10 seconds remaining to turn a 20-17 Tennessee lead into a 24-20 Philadelphia victory. The Titans, who looked completely lost last week in a 23-10 loss to the New York Jets, had the reigning NFC East champions on the ropes for much of the afternoon.

Philadelphia's problems started immediately. Star running back Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger on the Eagles' first offensive play and spent most of the first half on the sideline. He returned after halftime wearing a neck roll, but finished with just four carries for nine yards and one catch for 11 yards.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

That opening possession lasted more than seven minutes and moved deep into Tennessee territory, but it ended in the worst possible way. Hurts tried to find DeVonta Smith in the end zone, but Amani Hooker intercepted the pass and returned it 92 yards to the Philadelphia 10-yard line. Four plays later, Cam Ward scored on a 1-yard quarterback sneak to give Tennessee a 7-0 lead.

The Eagles responded with a 2-yard touchdown run from Tank Bigsby and Hurts connected with Smith for a 22-yard touchdown late in the second quarter. But the Titans refused to go away. Joey Slye kicked a 37-yard field goal just as time expired in the first half, cutting Philadelphia's lead to 14-10.

Jake Elliott extended the lead with a 58-yard field goal in the third quarter, but Ward scored his second rushing touchdown of the game to tie the score at 17.

Philadelphia had an opportunity to take control in the fourth quarter, but Hurts threw his second interception with just over six minutes remaining. The Titans responded with a 69-yard drive that included a 41-yard completion from Ward to Elic Ayomanor and a 27-yard run by Tyjae Spears on third-and-22.

The Eagles' defense eventually held Tennessee to a 33-yard field goal, but that still gave the Titans a three-point lead with 1:56 remaining and Philadelphia had no timeouts.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

That's when Hurts finally looked like the quarterback who led the Eagles to a Super Bowl victory in February 2025.

The 28-year-old signal-caller converted a third-and-6 with a 20-yard completion to Dontayvion Wicks and connected with Smith three times for 34 yards on the drive. Smith's final catch was a sweet grab along the sideline where he barely got his second foot down inbounds. The crucial play went for 19 yards and set the Eagles up at the Tennessee 3-yard line with 20 seconds remaining.

Two plays later, Hurts found Cooper for the game-winning touchdown, the first touchdown catch of Cooper’s NFL career.

Hurts finished 26-of-37 for 264 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. Smith caught 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown, accounting for nearly half of Philadelphia's passing production. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Smith has to step up as the team's top receiver, and he looked the part against Tennessee.

AJ BROWN SAYS THERE'S BEEN SILENCE BETWEEN HIM AND EX-TEAMMATE JALEN HURTS SINCE HIS MOVE TO NEW ENGLAND

Ward completed 13-of-20 passes for 183 yards and didn't turn the ball over, while adding both of Tennessee's touchdowns on the ground. It wasn't an especially good performance for the Titans offense, as the Eagles outgained Tennessee 341-291 and out-possessed the Titans by nearly 13 minutes.

The problem for Hurts and the Eagles was the two turnovers and general sloppy play at key moments.

Obviously, it’s hard to panic about a team that won its first two games. But if I were an Eagles fan, I’d feel about as nervous as possible for someone whose team is 2-0.

Philadelphia has beaten Washington and Tennessee by a combined six points. The Commanders might be better than people expected, but the Titans entered Sunday looking like one of the worst teams in football. The Eagles needed a touchdown with nine seconds remaining to beat them.

Good teams find ways to win close games, and Hurts deserves credit for helping the team survive back-to-back upset bids. But a supposed NFC contender cannot continue playing like this and expect to keep escaping.

The standings say the Eagles are perfect. Their play on the field has been anything but.

item.title: McDonald’s once sold beloved cookies featuring forgotten characters from the chain's past
item.description: McDonald's discontinued McDonaldland Cookies featured Grimace and Ronald McDonald faces with a subtle lemon flavor that fans still crave decades later.
item.content:encoded:
Introduced in 1974, McDonaldland Cookies became a regular addition to McDonald’s Happy Meals when they debuted nationwide in 1979, but the beloved menu item was discontinued in the early 2000s, to the disappointment of many fans.

The small, crunchy, cookies were baked for McDonald’s by Keebler, had a subtle lemon flavor and featured the faces of beloved McDonald’s characters like Grimace, Ronald McDonald, Birdie, and Hamburglar.

Customers described them as a cross between shortbread and animal crackers, and McDonaldland Cookies came in either a little plastic bag or a brightly colored cardboard box that also showed the faces of McDonald’s characters.

The fast food chain altered its Happy Meals to include healthier items such as apple slices in the early 2000s.

MCDONALD'S REVIVES DECADES-OLD FAVORITE FOR AMERICA 250 AFTER YEARS OF CUSTOMER REQUESTS

Between 2003 and 2004, McDonaldland Cookies were discontinued at all U.S. locations.

Chocolate chip cookies, however, remained on the menu.

McDonald’s has been serving some variation of chocolate chip cookies since the early 1970s, with today's chewy, soft-baked version introduced in 2012.

MCDONALD'S BRINGS BACK POPULAR ITEM FOR SHORT TIME AS ONE STATE GETS A TREAT

Although McDonaldland Cookies are no longer available in the United States, select McDonald’s locations in Australia still offer them, and certain New Zealand restaurants serve the treat under the name "McHappy Cookies."

Fans have also shared on Reddit that a cookie with a flavor and texture similar to the original McDonaldland cookies is available at Aldi supermarkets.

AMERICA'S FAVORITE FAST-FOOD CHAIN NAMED: MCDONALD'S WINS HEARTS BUT NOT BEST BURGER, SURVEY SAYS

One Reddit user commented: "I am eating the Benton's animal crackers from Aldi right now and they taste exactly like the McDonaldland cookies."

McDonaldland Cookies might be gone in the U.S., but the characters have not been totally forgotten.

The viral Grimace Shake, a purple-hued milkshake with a vanilla soft serve base and mixed berry flavoring, came out in 2023 as a limited-time treat to celebrate the beloved character’s birthday.

Beginning in 2022, McDonald's sporadically released various limited-edition Adult Happy Meals, allowing grownups to enjoy the nostalgia of Happy Meals — which, depending on their age, might have included McDonaldland Cookies.

Fox News Digital reached out to McDonald's for comment.

item.title: Keenan Allen faces NFL suspension after blood alcohol level nearly triple the legal limit: report
item.description: Keenan Allen's blood alcohol level was nearly triple the legal limit, which should trigger the NFL's substance abuse policy and potential suspension.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL could be dishing out a suspension to Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen after he was charged this week with two misdemeanors stemming from his arrest on charges of drunk driving before the start of the season.

Allen is facing preliminary charges of operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated (OVWI) as well as OVWI endangering a person, which are both misdemeanors in Indiana.

item.title: Massage clients report bizarre flu-like reaction after popular spa treatment
item.description: Massage flu symptoms like soreness, fatigue and headaches are real, but experts debunk the popular claim that massages release toxins from the body.
item.content:encoded:
A popular wellness treatment is allegedly leaving some people with unexpected symptoms, including aches, fatigue and headaches.

Social media users have described feeling under the weather after getting a massage, with some saying they feel as though they are coming down with an illness.

The reaction is sometimes referred to online as "massage flu," though health experts say it is not an actual medical diagnosis.

DO RED LIGHT THERAPY AND COLD PLUNGES REALLY WORK? A DOCTOR REVEALS THE TRUTH

"This phenomenon is something I have definitely heard of and had patients tell me," W. Zach Smith, a Seattle-based physical therapist and co-founder of HIDEF Physical Therapy, told Fox News Digital.

"The idea of this has been around a long time but usually described as fatigue and soreness," Smith said. "The flu part of the name I have heard more recently."

Soreness can happen when a lot of pressure is applied to the muscles for a long period of time, especially if someone is not used to getting massages, Smith added.

"Any time you go in and apply a lot of pressure to a muscle for a long period of time, it can essentially bruise the tissue," he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The body may also have a mild inflammatory response after a massage, which can contribute to soreness, Smith said.

Drew Voelsch, a chiropractor at Forza Chiropractic in Illinois, said he has also heard patients refer to the reaction as "massage flu" or an "adjustment hangover."

"The symptoms are real," Voelsch told Fox News Digital, pointing to soreness, fatigue and mild headaches that may last 24 to 48 hours. "The label is social media."

A massage around the neck, scalp or jaw can also trigger headaches because those areas can be involved in tension headaches, according to Smith.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Both experts pushed back on the idea that these symptoms are caused by a massage "releasing toxins" from the body, a claim that has circulated in social media comments.

"This is a myth," Smith said. "There is no basis or science behind this."

Voelsch agreed, noting that the liver and kidneys handle the body's waste-removal processes.

To help reduce discomfort, Smith recommended asking for less pressure or a shorter massage and gradually working up to deeper or longer sessions.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Voelsch also suggested drinking water, eating something light beforehand and moving gently afterward.

Mild soreness is typically not a cause for concern, but Smith said new or persistent pain may be a reason to contact a doctor.

"If you are having a new, unexplained pain that is persistent, that would be a good time to call your doctor," he said.

Voelsch recommended seeking medical advice if symptoms last longer than about 72 hours or include fever, sharp or radiating pain, numbness or tingling, spreading swelling or bruising, or faintness.

item.title: ICE shooting rocks Austin as Democrat demands bodycam video, independent probe
item.description: Austin police say a brief foot pursuit involving ICE ended with an adult man shot once in the torso and hospitalized in serious but stable condition.
item.content:encoded:
An ICE officer shot a man in Austin, Texas, on Sunday, prompting a crowd of angry demonstrators to gather near the scene, hurl obscenities and clash with authorities.

Department of Homeland Security (DHS) sources confirmed to Fox News that the man shot by the ICE officer is an illegal immigrant from Venezuela with a final order of removal.

Video from the scene showed people holding up their phones and carrying flags as the commotion unfolded. Police said preliminary information indicated the man was shot once in the torso during a brief foot pursuit involving ICE. He remained hospitalized in serious but stable condition.

Austin Mayor Kirk Watson, Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis and Austin-Travis County EMS Chief Robert Luckritz confirmed ICE was involved in the shooting and provided what they repeatedly stressed were preliminary details during a Sunday afternoon news conference.

Austin-Travis County EMS was notified of the shooting at approximately 12:56 p.m. and arrived in less than five minutes, Luckritz said. The adult man was taken from the scene within nine minutes and transported to a local trauma center in serious but stable condition after being shot once in the torso.

Davis said preliminary information indicated there was a brief foot pursuit before the shooting, but cautioned that she had not yet been briefed by federal authorities.

'SQUAD' MEMBER CALLS DHS 'GREATEST THREAT TO OUR SAFETY' AFTER ICE-INVOLVED SHOOTING

"From what I'm hearing, there was a small foot pursuit," Davis said. "But again, this is all very preliminary."

Watson stressed that the information available was "extremely preliminary." He said city officials wanted to make themselves available as quickly as possible when they had information, but warned against rushing to conclusions based on early claims circulating on TikTok, X and other social media platforms.

Watson added that the Austin Police Department was not involved in the shooting and only assisted with traffic control. APD's Special Investigations Unit and the Texas Rangers will work together to investigate the incident, Davis said.

"The city of Austin deserves answers," Davis said. "We're going to get all those questions answered, and we'll be as transparent as we can be."

Watson said he was "very angry" and "extremely unhappy" about the shooting, while accusing ICE of creating fear and chaos in Austin and other cities. He also questioned the agency's ability to investigate itself without local involvement.

ICE AGENTS IN FATAL HOUSTON SHOOTING WERE NOT WEARING BODY CAMERAS, SOURCES SAY

Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, claimed in a post on X that "ICE has shot a person in Austin this morning" and called for a full, independent investigation and the immediate release of body-camera footage.

"Over and over, ICE has shot people and then lied about what happened," Casar wrote. "We will demand truth, transparency and accountability."

During the news conference, Casar called the incident part of a "disturbing pattern" and said ICE's conduct "has got to stop."

"They've arrested 5-year-olds ... and now someone has been shot," Casar said. "This has got to stop."

Authorities have not identified the man who was shot or fully disclosed what led to the encounter.

The Austin investigation comes amid heightened tensions over federal immigration enforcement operations across the country.

ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS CLASH WITH AGENTS OUTSIDE NEW JERSEY DETENTION CENTER AS GOV SHERRILL DENIED ENTRY

Clashes erupted outside New Jersey's Delaney Hall immigration detention center in May after protesters defied a state police order to move to a designated demonstration area. Newark Mayor Ras Baraka later criticized the tactics used by state troopers sent to secure the facility, which had become the focus of frequent demonstrations.

Federal immigration operations also drew national scrutiny in Minnesota following the fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis. Good was killed by an ICE agent in early January after authorities said she tried to use her vehicle to run over federal officers, while Pretti was fatally shot by agents on Jan. 24 as he recorded federal officers.

Fox News Digital reached out to ICE and the Texas Department of Public Safety for additional information and comment.

item.title: Trump, Iranian president converge on NYC for ‘dramatic’ UN showdown as Tehran faces tight restrictions
item.description: President Donald Trump and Masoud Pezeshkian converge on New York City for the U.N. General Assembly amid strict U.S. restrictions on Iran's delegation movements.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are set to converge on New York City for the U.N. General Assembly (UNGA) this week, setting up what former White House officials describe as a "dramatic" diplomatic moment, with Tehran’s delegation effectively "captive" under U.S. restrictions amid heightened Middle East tensions.

Pezeshkian, for one, is scheduled to address the assembly on Wednesday, Reuters and Iran's semi-official news agency, Mehr, reported Sunday, with Trump at the rostrum on Tuesday.

"The choreography here is going to make for a fairly dramatic moment," Theo Wold, former acting assistant attorney general and White House domestic policy advisor, told Fox News Digital.

PUTIN, XI AND IRAN'S PEZESHKIAN DESCEND ON INDIA FOR HIGH-STAKES BRICS SUMMIT AMID ESCALATING GLOBAL TENSIONS

"For the Iranians, the limitation is going to be that there's going to be less access to the international press and less ability for them to essentially poke the Trump administration in the eye," Wold added before noting that it is "pretty sensible to allow them to participate in the international forum and to discuss whatever issues they think are pertinent to their regime and then tell them to go home."

The high-profile gathering also comes as Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran amid the almost seven-month war. Tehran, meanwhile, has set seven conditions for talks with Washington, according to Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei.

Iran also warned on Sunday against any big new attack by the United States and its allies, saying it had information such a move was being prepared, Reuters reported.

While the U.S. approved visas for Iran’s delegation earlier this week, including Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, the State Department has placed strict limits on Iranian movements while in Manhattan.

As the host country under a 1947 U.N. agreement, the United States generally must facilitate the entry and transit of foreign representatives traveling to U.N. headquarters, including officials from adversarial nations.

"While ordinary Iranians endure brutal repression, water and electricity shortages, and soaring inflation, the regime's officials want to go on shopping sprees in New York. Not on our watch," U.S. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said on X.

UN WATCHDOG SLAMS POTENTIAL ELECTION OF IRAN TO PANEL WITH HUMAN RIGHTS SWAY: 'LUNATICS RUNNING THE ASYLUM'

For Washington, Wold said the U.S. is not obligated to give them unrestricted access beyond diplomatic responsibilities.

"Here, the delegation will be restricted to their accommodation in New York City and the U.N. headquarters there in Manhattan," Wold clarified.

He characterized the move by Washington as a way of telling the delegation it could participate in official discussions but not "go and buy a bunch of microwaves or a small car at Costco or a dealership in the greater New York area."

"Some of the restrictions fully recognize that when Iran comes to New York for UNGA, really it's about them lining their pockets and going on shopping sprees to get household appliances and Rolex watches," Wold said. "They're not going to be going on shopping sprees. They're certainly not going to be hitting up Michelin-starred restaurants in greater Manhattan.

"They also go to Sam’s Club and Walmart and Costco. And that was one of the specific prohibitions issued by the State Department this week: to contact those big-box retailers that require a basic membership and say, ‘You’re not to transact or do any business with Iranians when they arrive, and you’re to notify us when they do.’"

KUSHNER TOUTS UNPRECEDENTED IRAN CONTACTS AS TEHRAN DENIES TRUMP BACKCHANNEL

Despite the restrictions, Wold said UNGA gives Washington the opportunity it has "wanted for quite some time to have a large enough audience, and a sort of captive Iranian delegation" to make some of the essential points for why the administration pursued the actions it did against the Iranian regime.

Iranian state media also reported Sept. 19 that Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said New York held "absolutely no charm" for the Iranian delegation.

Baghaei, Mehr News Agency reported, went on to accuse the U.S. of using every tool to block the delegation’s participation, asserting that Iran’s attendance is a legal right rather than a favor.

Wold went on to criticize the U.N. for hosting state representatives hostile to American interests while raising security concerns.

"It's going to be one of those things that's fairly perplexing to most Americans," Wold said. "How is it that the representatives of what we have long identified as a hostile regime, but now one that we're actually engaged in combat operations against, one that has killed American service members, why is it that their diplomats get to come to the United Nations and exchange niceties with other kleptocrats or some of their other allies on the international scene?"

TWO US SERVICE MEMBERS KILLED IN IRANIAN STRIKES ON JORDAN, CENTCOM SAYS

Wold also added that the United Nations wants to "lecture us about international climate change or the need to trans children, but the other is happy to sort of serve as a forum for obvious violators of human rights and obvious regimes that are contrary to any number of internationally agreed-upon protocols."

Amid the hostility between Washington and Tehran, Wold said the gathering could also provide an opening for diplomacy. Trump is also slated to hold bilateral and sideline meetings with leaders from the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) to discuss regional security and the Strait of Hormuz.

"There's the hope that there'll be an opportunity for real discussion," Wold said of UNGA. "Everyone's hope, especially from State Department leadership, is that there'll be an opportunity to have a fulsome, sort of meaningful discussion with the Iranians, freed from some of the theatrics the Iranians have engaged in.

"There's a hope that there'll be an opportunity for closed-door private discussions between the United States and Iranians and really try to hammer out some kind of agreement about what a cessation of hostilities will look like."

Wold expressed confidence in Washington’s posture heading into the summit.

"The president is best equipped for these moments. This is really where he sort of shines as a natural leader," he said. "He's not one to bend or to break. It's a precarious time for President Trump, but I have no doubt at all that he'll rise to the moment."

item.title: Massachusetts' plan to offer postpartum screening home visits sparks online debate
item.description: Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey is investing $2.25 million to send nurses into homes of new parents, sparking a heated government overreach debate.
item.content:encoded:
Massachusetts is expanding a taxpayer-funded program that sends nurses into the homes of new parents after childbirth, fueling debate over the government's role in family health care.

Gov. Maura Healey recently announced plans to invest $2 million to expand the state's Welcome Family program, which offers voluntary home visits from registered nurses after the birth of a child. Healey also proposed an additional $250,000 to strengthen the Massachusetts Child Psychiatry Access Program for Moms, which provides mental health support to providers caring for pregnant and postpartum patients.

"Everybody in the state, when you have a baby, you're going to have a home visit within days, weeks and that will be an opportunity for a healthcare provider to make an assessment to see if you need some additional support and resources," Healey said during an interview last week on Boston Public Radio.

CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR TAPS FORMER TRUMP LAWYER TO FIGHT BACK AS HE'S 'DRAGGED THROUGH THE MUD': ATTORNEY

Healey also said the state is investing in training healthcare providers to better identify the signs of postpartum mental health conditions.

The announcement comes amid heightened public attention to postpartum mental health in Massachusetts during the high-profile trial of Lindsay Clancy, the former labor and delivery nurse accused of killing her three young children in January 2023. In a case ultimately declared a mistrial because of a deadlocked jury, Clancy's defense argued she was suffering from severe postpartum mental illness. The case has reignited debate over how postpartum mental health conditions are identified and treated.

LINDSAY CLANCY'S FAMILY WAS 'VERY CONCERNED' ABOUT HER MENTAL HEALTH IN THE MONTHS BEFORE SHE KILLED HER KIDS

State officials say the program is intended to improve maternal health outcomes by connecting families with additional support.

The announcement also sparked debate on social media, where some users questioned whether the program represented an appropriate role for government. "Doctors and pediatricians are more than capable to conduct appropriate screenings for their patients. Say no to home visits," one user wrote on X, while another called the program "creepy" and "massive government overreach."

Not everyone opposed the proposal outright. "More overreach. However, if it's an offer, and not a mandate, it could be a good thing for some young families and single moms," comedian Bob Phillips wrote on X.

The reaction reflects a broader national debate over how states should balance maternal mental health, taxpayer costs, individual privacy and the role government should play in supporting new families.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Massachusetts Department of Public Health and Healey's office for additional comment.

CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS – NOT THE CCP – TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE

"Xi Jinping is facing a turbulent Communist Party at home, which means that he can't compromise. Also, he's arrogant. He incorrectly believes that China's on the way up and the United States is on the way down and we're in terminal decline," Chang explained.

"Homecoming is not a free pass to damage someone else's property or disrupt their quality of life," the department wrote on Facebook.

Quarterback Joe Burrow and the Bengals used that momentum to go 81 yards downfield for the first score of the game, and it was all thanks to Chase’s outstanding hands.

item.title: Ms Rachel calls Gaza journalist ‘friend’ in resurfaced clip after he admits hiding Oct 7 hostage footage
item.description: Children's YouTube star Ms. Rachel faces scrutiny after a resurfaced video shows her calling Motaz Azaiza her "friend" amid his Oct. 7 revelations.
item.content:encoded:
Children's YouTube star Ms. Rachel faced renewed scrutiny on Sunday after a 2025 video of her calling Palestinian photojournalist Motaz Azaiza her "friend," resurfaced, days after Azaiza admitted he deliberately withheld footage of Israeli hostages being beaten by a crowd in Gaza on Oct. 7, 2023.

The short video appears to show Ms. Rachel, whose real name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, introducing Azaiza to her young audience while teaching the letter "M."

"Hi, yes, it’s M, for my friend, Motaz. Yay! Bye!" Accurso said.

MS RACHEL CONFRONTED ON ACCUSING ISRAEL OF 'GENOCIDE' IN PARK INTERACTION WITH PODCASTER

The video was originally shared on Instagram and later removed, according to reporting from July 2025.

Azaiza, who amassed millions of social media followers documenting the war in Gaza, appeared briefly in the clip and greeted Ms. Rachel.

The video also took on new significance after Azaiza described earlier this month what he witnessed during the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, terrorist attack in an extensive interview with journalist Ahmed al-Biqawi on the Arabic-language "Taqarrab" podcast. Azaiza said he followed a vehicle carrying Israeli captives and filmed as members of a crowd assaulted them.

Azaiza said he didn't publish the video, however, as he feared it could put the Palestinians involved at risk.

"I saw the vehicle of the Al-Qassam Brigades, and there were Israeli captives there," Azaiza said. "People got out, watched, beat them, hit them, and I followed them and filmed. But I did not publish those videos. Why? Because I did not want to ruin the lives of the people who were filmed."

MS RACHEL POSTS SUPPORT FOR HIJAB-WEARING KINDERGARTNERS AFTER TRUMP POST

Azaiza said he withheld the footage because he believed Israeli authorities could use it to identify the Palestinians appearing in the videos.

"I understood that Israel would use those videos to identify every person who was there and eliminate them," Azaiza said. "I did not want to be responsible, even indirectly, for the deaths of those people in exchange for a few likes and views online."

NEW YORK TIMES ISSUES CORRECTION, DELETES LINE QUESTIONING IF ISRAELIS WERE VICTIMS OF OCT 7 TERROR ATTACK

Azaiza also criticized Hamas and described the restrictions faced by journalists working inside Gaza. He said photographers learned to lower their cameras when Palestinians criticized Hamas because showing such dissent could lead to retaliation.

Despite describing himself as a supporter of armed Palestinian resistance, Azaiza said Hamas' actions had failed to protect Palestinians living in Gaza.

"I support armed resistance, but one that brings results, or at least gives me the feeling that my life is valuable in the eyes of the resistance," Azaiza said. "Why should a Palestinian be cheap in the eyes of Palestinians themselves? You are making people hate the resistance with your own hands."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE
 

Azaiza's profile rose dramatically after the war began. Time named him to its 2024 list of the world's 100 most influential people for his photographs documenting Gaza.

Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, told Fox News Digital that Azaiza’s disclosure raised questions about his journalistic judgment and his decision to withhold the footage.

"After years spent claiming to share what was happening in Gaza ‘unfiltered,’ Azaiza revealed that he hid footage — not, per journalistic norms, to protect victims from further harm, but because he didn't want Israel to arrest the perpetrators. Innocent civilians had been kidnapped, already sexually abused, and his concern was with the people that beat them and rejoiced at Hamas' crimes. That speaks volumes about his journalism and his moral character," Menken said.

Accurso, meanwhile, has become increasingly outspoken about Gaza.

Last week, she accused celebrities and other public figures who had remained silent about Palestinian children of applying a racial double standard.

"They probably would say something if these kids were White and from a different place," Accurso said. "Please stop being racist and risk something."

Elizabeth Barcohana, the California Republican Party’s Jewish engagement chair, told Fox News Digital that she believed Accurso’s Gaza advocacy was spreading misleading information to her large audience.

"Ms. Rachel is essentially sanitizing terrorism with false and misleading information to emotionally manipulate her very impressionable following and those around her in her industry," Barcohana said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Ms. Rachel for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Fat Bear Week bracket is set: meet the heavyweights, underdogs and defending champ in this year's tournament
item.description: Forget March Madness. Fat Bear Week returns to Katmai National Park with 16 brown bears as defending champ Chunk faces rising star Bucky on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Forget March Madness. The most important bracket of the year has arrived.

Fat Bear Week is back, baby!

The annual competition at Alaska's Katmai National Park and Preserve kicks off Tuesday with 16 brown bears vying for the title of chonkiest champ. This year's bracket features a defending champion, a few rising stars and some heavyweight opening-round matchups.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

Here's how it works: Two bears face off in a single-elimination tournament, and fans vote for the one they believe has done the best job packing on the pounds ahead of winter hibernation.

More than 1.7 million votes were cast during last year's competition, which saw Bear 32 — better known as "Chunk" — claim the title.

Now, the reigning champ is back for another shot at glory. But he's got some serious competition.

Chunk won last year's competition despite suffering a broken jaw in June 2025, likely during a fight with another bear. The injury left him with a distinctive scar and protruding canine tooth, but it apparently didn't slow down his appetite.

This summer, Chunk was largely absent from Brooks River during the salmon run before returning in September with a substantial belly. Park officials aren't sure where he spent most of his summer. But wherever he was, he wasn't skipping meals.

And he's going to need every pound. His title defense begins Wednesday against Bear 164, Bucky, one of the river's emerging heavyweights.

Bucky has grown considerably in recent years, developing the size and confidence to challenge other dominant males for access to the best fishing spots.

He's also figured out a pretty clever way to keep himself fed.

While other bears compete for the same prime real estate at Brooks Falls, Bucky has learned to position himself near the waterfall's deepest plunge pool, where he can catch salmon jumping through the air, rising from below or falling from above.

And at approximately 9 years old, Bucky is still relatively young. Male brown bears typically reach their physical prime between ages 12 and 20, so he could have several more years of growth ahead of him.

The rising star gets his shot at the defending champion Wednesday, Sept. 23. One of them will be going home early.

Well, metaphorically. They'll both still be in Alaska eating fish.

Bear 151, Walker, used to be a relatively easygoing guy who enjoyed playing with other bears. As he's gotten older, though, he's become a little grumpier and a lot more competitive.

And the younger bears are giving him plenty of reasons to be grumpy.

WILDLIFE PHOTOGRAPHER STAYS ICE-COLD AS MASSIVE BROWN BEAR WALKS RIGHT UP TO HIS CAMERA

Bucky and Bear 903, Gully, have been challenging Walker's position in the Brooks River hierarchy. His size and experience have helped him maintain his standing, but the younger competition is catching up.

Walker faces Gully in Wednesday's opening round, giving us another veteran-versus-youngster matchup right out of the gate.

Check out the rump on this guy, by the way.

Bear 610 might not be one of the biggest competitors in this year's field, but she's got a pretty compelling story.

When she was first identified in 2015, park officials believed she had separated from her mother earlier than expected. She also had a significant healing wound above her hips, suggesting she'd survived an attack.

Now, more than a decade later, she's raising her first known litter of cubs.

Despite being a relatively small, first-time mother, 610 has successfully protected and cared for both cubs throughout the summer while building up her own fat reserves ahead of hibernation.

This is her first Fat Bear Week appearance, and she'll face Bear 89, Backpack, in Wednesday's opening round.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Of course, Fat Bear Week isn't just about which bear has the biggest belly. The competition celebrates the remarkable transformations these animals undergo as they prepare to survive months of winter hibernation without eating or drinking.

The opening round takes place Sept. 22–23, followed by the quarterfinals Sept. 24–25, the Final Fat Four on Sept. 28 and the championship on Sept. 29.

You can view the complete bracket and cast your votes on the official Fat Bear Week website. Voting is open from noon to 9 p.m. ET on tournament days.

item.title: Week 3 AP Top 25 poll reflects just how deep the SEC is this season with 10 teams represented
item.description: Ole Miss surges into the AP Poll top 5 after its revenge win over LSU, while an impressive 10 SEC teams are ranked heading into a loaded week 4.
item.content:encoded:
Week 3 of the college football season is in the books, and as we head into a monster week of matchups around the sport, we've got a brand-new AP Poll to dive into.

Ole Miss getting its revenge on Lane Kiffin and his LSU team in Oxford on Saturday night not only lived up to every expectation imaginable as one of the most highly anticipated games in recent history, but it also resulted in the unbeaten Rebels getting a boost into the Top 5 of the AP Poll.

Mississippi State technically took the biggest leap of teams inside the Top 25, going from unranked a week ago to No. 24 after its road win over South Carolina. As for the biggest fall, that belongs to Texas A&M after the Aggies suffered what most would categorize as a shocking home upset against Kentucky.

The Top 3 teams remained unchanged from a week ago, with Texas maintaining the top spot as the Longhorns continue to own the most impressive win of the young season after taking down Ohio State in Week 2.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The glaring takeaway from this week's AP Poll is just how well represented the SEC is.

Even with their loss on the road at Ole Miss, the LSU Tigers still occupy the No. 10 spot to round out a Top 10 featuring five teams from the Southeastern Conference. With Florida and Mississippi State also joining the Top 25 party, a grand total of 10 SEC teams are represented.

The Big Ten, meanwhile, has seven teams ranked inside the Top 25 heading into Week 4.

Speaking of Week 4, it featured a loaded docket of must-see games that will surely have quite an impact on College Football Playoff dreams for programs around the country.

It's a long list of marquee matchups: No. 14 Tennessee plays host to No. 1 Texas, No. 4 Ole Miss travels to No. 21 Florida, No. 10 LSU hosts No. 23 Texas A&M, No. 24 Mississippi State hosts No. 19 Missouri, No. 17 Iowa travels to No. 18 Michigan, and No. 12 USC plays host to No. 20 Oregon, just to name a handful.

While there were quite a number of moving pieces in the Week 3 poll, next week's poll has the makings of being a real doozy.

item.title: America and China are fighting for the future of AI — chips are the battlefield
item.description: President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet in Washington as Huawei races to build a rival AI chip ecosystem that could displace American semiconductor dominance.
item.content:encoded:
When President Donald Trump sits down with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington this week, the agenda will be crowded.

Trade. Tariffs. Rare earth minerals. National security. Supply chains.

But looming over all of it is a technological competition that could shape the balance of economic and military power for decades: artificial intelligence. And increasingly, the battle isn't simply about who builds the best AI model.

TRUMP-XI’S CHINA SUMMIT IS A DEFINING TEST FOR AMERICA IN THE NEW COLD WAR

It is about who controls the chips, computing infrastructure and technology ecosystem underneath it.

America remains the global leader in advanced AI technology and semiconductor design. But China is pushing aggressively to reduce its dependence on American technology, and Huawei has emerged as one of the most important companies in that effort. That should have Washington's full attention.

For years, the United States has used export controls to restrict China's access to advanced semiconductors and semiconductor-manufacturing technology, particularly technologies with potential military applications.

Those restrictions had a clear national-security objective: prevent America's most sophisticated technology from strengthening a strategic competitor's military capabilities. But there has also been an unintended consequence worth confronting. China accelerated its effort to build an AI ecosystem that doesn't need America.

AI 'DOOMERS' RISK KNEECAPPING US VS CHINA, BUT EX-PENTAGON VET SAYS BOTH EXTREMES MISS THE MARK

Huawei expanded its Ascend AI-chip roadmap. Chinese developers adapted software and models to domestic hardware. Chinese companies poured resources into computing systems capable of compensating for some of the performance limitations of individual Chinese chips. And Huawei isn't standing still.

The company recently said demand for its AI computing equipment in China is exceeding supply. It is accelerating future generations of its Ascend processors and developing enormous computing systems capable of connecting vast numbers of chips.

That means the strategic question facing Washington has changed.

AMERICA RUNS ON DATA. IF WE DON’T BUILD THE INFRASTRUCTURE, CHINA WILL

The question isn't simply: How do we keep sensitive American technology away from China? It is also: How do we make sure the rest of the world continues choosing American technology instead of China's? Those are related questions, but they aren't identical.

If American technology becomes inaccessible across too much of the global market, China has an enormous incentive to develop substitutes. Huawei has an enormous incentive to sell them. And governments and companies around the world have an enormous incentive to build around whatever technology they can reliably obtain.

THE AI REVOLUTION COULD BECOME A NATIONAL SECURITY DISASTER IF WE AREN'T CAREFUL

Once developers write software for an ecosystem, companies construct computing infrastructure around it and countries invest billions deploying it, switching becomes much harder. That's why this isn't merely a chip-sales competition. It is an ecosystem competition.

America wants a world running on American chips, American software, American standards and American innovation. China wants to build an alternative. It wants a world in which Huawei and other Chinese companies provide a technology stack that Beijing controls and America cannot easily influence.

President Trump has taken a different approach from the Biden administration. His administration rescinded the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule while maintaining controls targeting technologies with serious national-security implications.

The administration has also allowed certain advanced chips to be considered for sale to approved Chinese customers under licensing requirements and security conditions. The theory is straightforward: protect the technologies most critical to national security without unnecessarily surrendering commercial markets to Chinese competitors. That distinction matters.

CHINA IS BUILDING AN AI WAR MACHINE. WASHINGTON MUST WAKE UP BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE

Nobody serious is arguing that America should simply hand China unrestricted access to technology that could materially enhance advanced weapons, military AI, surveillance or other sensitive capabilities.

National security comes first. But there is a difference between protecting America's crown-jewel technology and adopting restrictions so sweeping that they accelerate China's determination to replace American technology throughout the commercial market. Because Huawei's goal isn't merely to survive American restrictions.

Huawei wants to compete. It wants Chinese chips powering Chinese AI. It wants Chinese computing infrastructure supporting Chinese models. And ultimately, Chinese technology companies want customers outside China using their systems.

That's why the next phase of this competition will be fought over which chips countries buy, which computing systems they install, which software developers learn and which technology stack becomes the default infrastructure for the AI economy.

America has enormous advantages. We have extraordinary semiconductor designers, the world's leading AI companies, deep capital markets, world-class universities, entrepreneurs and an innovation culture China has spent decades trying to replicate.

But technological leadership isn't permanent. It has to be defended. And sometimes the greatest threat to American leadership isn't that China suddenly invents something better. It's that America creates policies that make its own technology harder for the world to use while Beijing aggressively offers an alternative.

There are already calls for the United States to slow AI development or impose broader restrictions in the name of safety and security. Those arguments deserve serious debate.

AI presents real risks. Advanced semiconductor technology has genuine military applications. Export controls can be an important national-security tool. But every restriction also has consequences.

The question should be whether a restriction actually improves American security without unnecessarily strengthening China's competing technology ecosystem. Because China isn't pausing. Huawei isn't pausing. And global demand for AI computing certainly isn't pausing.

Somebody will provide the chips. Somebody will provide the computing infrastructure. Somebody will provide the software. Somebody will establish the standards.

The United States has a direct strategic interest in American companies remaining central to that ecosystem.

The previous generation of American leaders watched too much manufacturing capacity and too many strategically important supply chains migrate overseas. We should not repeat that mistake with the infrastructure of artificial intelligence.

Semiconductors are no longer merely components inside computers. Compute is strategic power.

The nations and companies controlling advanced computing will possess enormous advantages in scientific discovery, medicine, manufacturing, intelligence, cybersecurity and military technology. That is why the Trump-Xi meeting matters far beyond whatever trade agreement or diplomatic communiqué emerges from Washington.

The two presidents represent countries competing over something much larger: Who builds the technological infrastructure of the 21st century?

The United States should protect its most sensitive technology, its intellectual property and technologies with significant military applications. At the same time, American companies will continue competing for commercial markets around the world.

Design the chips here. Build the semiconductor infrastructure here. Develop the software here. Protect the technology that truly must be protected. And keep American technology innovative and competitive enough that countries around the world continue choosing the American ecosystem instead of Huawei's.

The AI Cold War is already underway. And the chips are the battlefield.
